composition.mass: Concentrated in the wide upper-half terraced mass matching the expanding jagged cranial silhouette.
composition.read: The viewer enters at the southern candle altar at row 9, tracing the narrow smoke path upward through the middle ground. The eye ascends into the calm lavender face of the effigy before being drawn upward into the jagged tiered plateau packed with colorful totems.

lighting.notes: flat graphic silkscreen illumination: Reflects the high-key periwinkle field of the canvas which illuminates the subject evenly without cast shadows.

rules: Keep the peripheral void totally unpopulated to preserve the clean poster-cardstock margin.
Cluster eyeball and helix totems symmetrically along the east and west outer tiers.
Confine smoke ribbon props strictly to the central path leading up to the effigy.
Elevate the northern crown to height 3 to emphasize the spiky cranial crest.

lens.aspect: Digital ink monoline contours, silkscreen vector flat color fills, and symmetrical doodle iconography.
lens.place: A floating vector dais shaped like a crowned psyche hovering in an endless periwinkle void.
lens.summary: The artwork's flat graphic linework and sharp silkscreen edges become clean geometric blocks, tiered ink-black cliffs, and bright enameled decorative totems.
lens.differs: Unlike painterly or organic landscape readings, every feature here is rendered as crisp, solid silkscreen shapes with bilateral symmetry and stark graphic contrast.

shaper.name: symmetric
shaper.why: Matches the drawing's strong bilateral vertical symmetry centered on the candle, nose, third eye, and radiating hair crown.

surface_mix.why: Paper-pale sand forms the smooth walkable floor, grass accents provide graphic mint fields, and stone pads cap out at 15% as pale lavender cobbles.

cliff_treatment.why: Translates the dense pitch-black silkscreen mass of the hair silhouette directly into stark, sharp-edged drop-offs.

lighting.why: Reflects the high-key periwinkle field of the canvas which illuminates the subject evenly without cast shadows.

concept.name: lens-medium
concept.fragment: LENS "medium": the artwork's MATERIAL AND MARKS become the island's physical character. Start from ANALYSIS.medium and ANALYSIS.palette, not from the subject. The ground is made of the marks: single-stroke ink becomes ribbon land and sweeping arcs of path with void where the paper is empty (shaper "ribbon", or "spiral" for a curl); airbrush gradients become soft radial terraces fading outward (shaper "radial"); fauvist or knife strokes become a patchwork of flat colour blocks at different heights (shaper "patchwork"); charcoal smudge becomes soft-edged dark masses with pale mist lying in the hollows (shaper "mound" or "basin"); pencil hatching or scratchy ink becomes angular slabs split by thin seams (shaper "shards"); vector doodles become dense small ornament on a tidy mirrored plan (shaper "symmetric"). Choose shaper params from the marks themselves (how many strokes, how wide, which way they sweep, how many blocks). Palette, surface_mix and cliff_treatment follow the medium (ink: paper-pale sand and ink-dark cliffs; airbrush: rings of surfaces fading by value; fauvist: saturated patches; charcoal: soft grey-green, mossy or soft cliffs). New props are the marks made solid: a brush flick as a curved blade of stone, a smudge as a low soft boulder, a doodle as a ring of beads, a knife stroke as a flat tilted slab. The figure's pose comes from how it is drawn (a single continuous stroke, a stack of colour patches), and it may be a monument of the marks rather than a living creature.
